description: Constant backend capacity below maxRate: AIMD oscillates around it in the classic TCP sawtooth.
A sudden capacity drop trips a band and cuts the rate into a lower sawtooth around the capacity.
After a capacity collapse and rate cut, restored capacity returns the backend to healthy and max.
Capacity recovers in steps; the limiter climbs back to a higher safe rate at each step.
Capacity flaps between healthy and degraded: compounding cuts ratchet the rate toward the floor.
Capacity steps down gradually; the limiter re-discovers a lower safe rate at each step.
A two-tier backend (soft + hard ceiling) produces two distinct failure levels across the bands.
Offered load starved below the sampling floor: with no measurements the limiter blindly doubles the rate (TCP slow-start) until load returns and the window fills.
